answer: We model Sybil resistance via a beacon-anchored dynamic opportunity-cost bond whose required stake spirals with verified identity multiplicity and a terrace of subgame-perfect slashing matrices enforcing grim-trigger punishment across colluding nodes. Because identity multiplication raises marginal bond cost above any discounted per-Sybil payoff, the expected net gain stays strictly negative, so deviation never survives equilibrium selection and honest single-identity participation constitutes a strict Nash equilibrium in adversarial multi-agent environments.
